claims.claim: Frank Mentzer's redline review of the Quagmire! rough draft objected that the text was padded.
claims.source: Jon Peterson, 'Quagmire! The Making of a 1980's D&D Module', Medium, 2014
claims.page: Development Hell Level 7: Rough Draft Consultation

claims.claim: Mentzer's review of the same draft also faulted it as extremely repetitive.
claims.source: Jon Peterson, 'Quagmire! The Making of a 1980's D&D Module', Medium, 2014

claims.claim: Mentzer objected to the redundant construction 'Patriarch Cleric' by likening it to 'female girl'.
claims.source: Jon Peterson, 'Quagmire!', Medium, 2014, reporting Mentzer's marginalia

claims.claim: Mentzer's consultation role was to ensure BECMI modules used the game's system terms consistently.
Every TSR module of the period had a product standards sheet fixing its styles, type sizes and margins.
claims.quote: listed all of the styles, typesizes, margins

claims.claim: Much of the flavor text that troubled Mentzer was cut from the published module.
claims.quote: including the saving throw notation and the flavor text

claims.claim: The module's section breakdown worksheet projected each section's length in both pages and lines of the HP3000 editor.
claims.quote: measured both by page count and by line count
claims.page: Development Hell Level 5: Design Crunch Time

claims.claim: TSR stripped city names from the player-facing map of Quagmire!, and withheld the pointer to the Spiral City itself.
claims.page: Development Hell Level 6: Maps and Illustrations

claims.claim: The front cover of a 1984 TSR module carried only a few sentences of flavor text beneath the cover illustration.
claims.quote: a few sentences of flavor text
